record.paper_title: Singularity Theorems in General Relativity: Achievements and Open Questions.
record.original_question: Can one formulate a singularity-theorem-style criterion based on the spatial averages of physical variables such as energy density or related matter fields, so that vanishing spatial averages distinguish singularity-free models permitted by the singularity theorems from models that still develop singularities?

evidence.quote: However, his work provided some inspiration, and I believe that the vanishing of the spatial averages of the physical variables is probably a condition which may allow to distinguish between the singularity-free models allowed by the singularity theorems and the singular ones. A conjecture of the singularity-theorem type was put forward in (Senovilla, 1998b) with this purpose.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a globally hyperbolic spacetime satisfying the standard energy and causality conditions appearing in the classical singularity theorems (e.g., the dominant energy condition and the strong/null energy condition), and let $\{\Sigma_t\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$ be a foliation of $M$ by spacelike Cauchy hypersurfaces with induced volume forms $d\mu_t$. For a scalar physical variable $\Phi$ on $M$ (such as the energy density $\rho = T_{\mu\nu}u^\mu u^\nu$ of a timelike congruence $u^\mu$, or any component of the energy–momentum or Ricci tensor projected along $u^\mu$), define its spatial average on $\Sigma_t$ by
$$\langle\Phi\rangle(t) \;=\; \lim_{V\to\infty}\frac{1}{V}\int_{B_t(V)} \Phi\, d\mu_t,$$
where $B_t(V)\subset\Sigma_t$ is an exhausting family of compact regions of volume $V$ (assuming $\Sigma_t$ is non-compact; otherwise take the integral over $\Sigma_t$ divided by its total volume).

Formulate and prove a singularity-theorem-style criterion of the following form: under the hypotheses of a classical singularity theorem (e.g., everywhere expanding open non-rotating cosmological model with matter satisfying the dominant energy condition), if the spatial average $\langle\rho\rangle(t)$ (or more generally the spatial average of every relevant component of the energy–momentum tensor) does not tend to zero as $t\to -\infty$ (or, equivalently, is bounded away from zero on a sequence of Cauchy slices), then $(M,g)$ is past timelike geodesically incomplete. Equivalently, show that any geodesically complete (singularity-free) solution within the relevant class must have vanishing spatial averages of the physical matter variables, thereby characterizing the known non-singular cosmological models among those allowed by the classical singularity theorems.
artifact.status_search_result: A singularity theorem of this type has been proved by Senovilla (gr-qc/0610127, Pramana 2007): for open, expanding, non-rotating cosmological models satisfying the dominant energy condition, a non-vanishing spatial average of the energy density (or of any component of the energy–momentum/Ricci tensor) implies past geodesic incompleteness. Thus the original conjecture is essentially established in this setting, while broader formulations (e.g., for rotating or anisotropic models, or for closed slices) remain only partially addressed.

status_evidence.title: A singularity theorem based on spatial averages
status_evidence.snippet: A singularity theorem based on spatial averages of physical variables is presented; non-vanishing spatial average of the energy density (or any component of the energy-momentum tensor) implies the existence of past singularities under the dominant energy condition.
status_evidence.claim: The spatial-averages conjecture has been proved as a singularity theorem in the open non-rotating expanding setting.

status_evidence.title: A singularity theorem based on spatial averages (Pramana)
status_evidence.snippet: Any singularity-free model must have a vanishing spatial average of the energy density (and other physical variables).
